turns.question: Why is there a big drop in pH on Sept 26?
turns.answer:
Here's what the pod actually recorded around Sept 26 — and note the day had both a spike and a crash:

**The sequence (times UTC)**
- Sept 24–25: pH steady around 7.4–7.5.
- 01:56 Sept 26: jumped from 8.12 to 11.83 in 30 minutes, then climbed to a peak of 12.91 around 06:26 【T1】.
- The drop you're asking about: 11.21 at 17:26 fell to 6.36 at 17:56 — about 4.9 units in half an hour, mid-morning local time. It then held near 7.0–7.2 for the rest of the day 【T2】.
- It fell again to 2.73 at 00:56 Sept 27, bottomed at 3.42 on Sept 28, and recovered to about 4.3 by the end of that day 【T1】.

**How the system flags it:** Against the operator's configured pH limits of 6–10, the pod was flagged high from 11:26–17:26 UTC on Sept 26 (highest 11.92) and low from 01:56 UTC Sept 27 to 23:30 UTC Sept 28 (lowest 3.418); both stretches have since cleared 【T1】. The system also marks 26 readings in this window as very unusual — sudden jumps and values "outside the range natural water spans" 【T1】. As general background only (not this pod's limit), uncontaminated fresh waters commonly "have a pH in the range of 6.5 to 8.5" 【3】.

**Why it happened:** The readings don't say. No readings were excluded as probe faults, so these stand as what the sensor recorded, and the data alone can't show the cause — a calibration check would confirm the unusual pH values. Two other metrics moved over the same hours: temperature climbed from about 67°F to 85°F and conductivity fell from about 71,000 to 58,400 µS/cm, while dissolved oxygen held near 8–9 mg/L and ORP eased from about 237 to 219 mV 【T3】. Turbidity can't add anything here — its readings have been stuck since Sept 11, which the device reports as a likely failed sensor that should be inspected 【T3】.

Data covered in this reply: Algalita Pod, 2026-09-24 00:00 to 2026-09-29 00:00 UTC (240 readings); Algalita Pod, 2026-09-26 00:00 to 2026-09-27 00:00 UTC (48 readings); Algalita Pod, 2026-09-26 00:00 to 2026-09-29 00:00 UTC (143 readings).

turns.question: Why is there a big drop in pH on Sept 26?
turns.answer:
Over Sept 24–28 the pH didn't simply drop on Sept 26 — it swung violently in both directions, and the device flagged the whole episode as an unusual stretch: 20 readings between Sept 26 02:26 UTC and Sept 27 00:56 UTC, spanning 2.73 to 12.91, kept in the record rather than excluded as faults 【T1】.

What the record shows (times in the pod's local solar time):

- Through Sept 25, pH held steady around 7.4–7.5.
- On the evening of Sept 25 (~18:00 local, 01:56 UTC Sept 26) it jumped from 8.12 to 11.83 in 30 minutes and kept climbing overnight, peaking near 12.9.
- Through the morning of Sept 26 it slid back — still ~11.8 mid-morning — then fell abruptly from 11.21 to 6.36 around 10:00 local (17:56 UTC).
- Late that afternoon (~17:00 local, 00:56 UTC Sept 27) it crashed to 2.73, then settled near 5.
- It kept sliding through Sept 27, bottoming at 3.418 on Sept 28, before recovering to ~4.3 by the end of Sept 28.

Against this pod's configured pH thresholds of 6–10, pH was flagged out of range — high on Sept 26 (up to 11.92) and low from Sept 27 into Sept 28 (down to 3.418). Both flags have since cleared 【T1】.

Other metrics moved at the same time: conductivity rose in step, from about 59,000–61,000 µS/cm to about 71,000 at the peak, and fell back as pH did; temperature swung from ~84°F down to ~67.7°F and back to ~85°F; ORP rose only slightly (~224 → ~239 mV).

As for why: the data shows what happened, but nothing in it can establish the cause. What I can say is that readings near 12.9 and 2.7 are, in the device's own description, outside the range natural water spans — for general background, uncontaminated river waters generally have a pH in the range of 6.5 to 8.5 【2】, though that is background, not a limit set for this salt-water site. A calibration check would confirm whether the pH sensor was reading true.

One separate caveat from this window: the pod's turbidity sensor has been stuck at a single value since Sept 11, which the system flags as a likely failed sensor that should be inspected 【T1】.
